p: seventh year: Of the captivity of Jeconiah.
them to know the abominations of: This declares the great leniency and patience of God who calls sinners to repentance before he condemns them.

lifted up my hand to the: I swore that I would be their God, which manner of oath was observed from all antiquity, where they used to lift up their hands toward the heavens, acknowledging God to be the author of truth and the defender of it, and also the judge of the heart, wishing that he would take vengeance, if they concealed anything which they knew to be truth.
and defile not yourselves with the: God had forbidden them to make mention of the idols, Ex 23:13, Ps 16:4.
their eyes: Which declares the wickedness of man's heart, who judge God's service by their eyes and outward senses.

name's sake: God had ever this respect to his glory, that he would not have evil spoken of his Name among the Gentiles for the punishment that his people deserved, in confidence of which the godly ever prayed, as in Ex 32:12, Nu 14:13.
nations: Who might by it take an opportunity to blaspheme my Name and to accuse me of lack of ability, or else that I had sought a means to destroy them more conveniently.
sabbaths: That is, my true religion, which I had commanded them, and gave themselves to serve me according to their own fantasies.

fathers: By which the Holy Spirit confuses them that say that they will follow the religion and example of their fathers, and not measure their doings by God's word whether they are approved by it or not.
their fathers' idols: Meaning that they set their delight on them.
them also statutes that were not: Because they would not obey my laws, I gave them up to themselves that they should obey their own fantasies, as in Eze 20:39, Ro 1:21,24.

gifts: I condemned those things, and counted them as abominable, which they thought had been excellent and to have declared most zeal, Lu 16:15 for that which God required as most excellent they gave to their idols.

For when I had brought them: Not only in the wilderness, when I brought them out of Egypt, but since I placed them in this land: which declares how prompt man's heart is to idolatry seeing that by no admonitions can he be drawn back.

Bamah to this day: Which signifies a high place, declaring that they vaunted themselves of their idolatry and were not ashamed of it, though God had commanded them expressly that they should have no altar lifted on high by stairs, Ex 20:26.
I will not be enquired of: He shows that the ingratitude of the people deserves that God should cut them off, and that they should not have the comfort of his word.

stone: He declares that man by nature is wholly enemy to God, and to his own salvation, and therefore God calls him to the right way, partly by chastising but chiefly by his mercy in forgiving his rebellion and wickedness.
wilderness of the people: I will bring you among strange nations as into a wilderness and there will visit you, and so call you to repentance and then bring the godly home again, Isa 65:9.
purge out from among you the: Signifying that he will not burn the corn with the chaff, but chose out the wicked to punish them when he will spare his.
Go ye: This is spoken to the hypocrites.
shall lothe yourselves in your own: Your own consciences will convict you after you have felt my mercies.
the south: For Judah stood south from Babylon.
green tree in thee: Both strong and weak in Jerusalem.
parables: The people said that the prophet spoke darkly: therefore he desires the Lord to give them a plain declaration of it.
